summary: Wrote and validated one update for this turn (validate: valid=true, no_change=false, execution_requested=false; effects: create source s-commitment-map; append interpretation for 7e10640e7212486b94a80f04b69febc2-question-1; append interpretation for 790eb5d64ed94ef5aea4736e6f66381d-question-0). It carries two additive, non-duplicating changes and requests no new execution. (1) The drafted-but-unapplied empty-configuration account is included so it is not lost: with an empty recovered configuration the node admits any transport-reachable sender on votes and on replication, and the live-cluster effect is bounded because appendEntries records whatever sender arrives as leader while the follower loop clears a known leader only when contact stops, so a restarted node sharing a cluster with a heartbeating legitimate leader converges back on it; that bound is stated as source-derived, with unmeasured multi-node behaviour carried as an explicit limitation. (2) A source-derived breadth check on the point left open for the leader-verification question (whether any other consumer of peer acknowledgements treats non-voters as counting): a newly anchored range in commitment.go (newCommitment, lines 29-46) builds the commitment map from the configuration's voters only and commitment.match() ignores any server not already a key, so a non-voter's replication acknowledgement cannot advance the commit index; checkLeaderLease filters on suffrage and quorumSize counts voters only. That narrows verifyLeader to the single acknowledgement consumer that admits a non-voter, with the breadth statement recorded as read from source rather than measured. No new hash, contract, baseline, gate or source modification was introduced; only draft/update.json was written (the prior pending payload was kept as draft/update.prev.json and its content is folded into the submission).
